data.title: Nvidia's stock has tumbled 27% over one chaotic month. The next big test lies in the week ahead
data.description:
By Bill Peters

Jensen Huang faces tough questions from Congress this week. Good luck pinning him down, an analyst says.

This handout photo posted on the official X account of Nvidia on Nov. 23 shows reinstated CEO of Nvidia Jensen Huang reacting to the ovation from employees upon his return to the company headquarters in Santa Clara, Calif.

After a month unlike any other for Nvidia, the chip maker at the heart of the artificial-intelligence boom and the stock market faces even more drama in the week ahead.

Newly-reinstated CEO Jensen Huang is set to face harsh questioning by U.S. lawmakers from both parties this week in Washington. During that stretch, Nvidia (NVDA) will also hold a large developer conference in the same city that could shed light on new products.

In both events, Nvidia will try to repair its image and articulate its path forward, after Huang resigned earlier this month following reports that he had extramarital affairs, including with a woman believed to be a spy for China.

Nvidia's stock has dropped 27% in November through Wednesday against that backdrop, which puts it on track for the worst monthly performance since it lost 32% in April 2022. That decline comes even after an 18.9% rally so far this week.

Huang's ouster, which lasted a little more than a week, initially lopped more than $1 trillion off Nvidia's market value. And it deepened concerns over national security, the lengths taken and possible exceptions made to restore Huang to his old job on Monday, and an economy and stock market seemingly dependent on one executive.

Huang is set to appear for closed-door transcribed interviews with three House committees on Tuesday. He will also appear before the Senate Committee on Banking, Housing and Urban Affairs on Thursday.

During those hearings, analysts say, lawmakers are almost certain to ask about Nvidia's relationship with China and the U.S. government, and what sensitive information Huang may have ultimately ended up handing over to China as that nation looks for a leg up in the global AI race. There will also likely be questions about what Nvidia knew, if anything, about China's alleged access to its high-end chips - via smuggling, routing them through other nations, or remote access - and the money behind it.

Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Jay Goldberg, an analyst at Seaport Research Partners who covers semiconductors, said that Huang appeared to have support among Nvidia's employees and shareholders. Attitudes in Congress - from Democrats worried about President Donald Trump and aggressive AI development to Republicans worried about economic threats from China - were more frigid.

"That that's the one thing that Democrats and Republicans can agree on, is that the greatest entrepreneur of all time is somehow a target," he said. "Not to excuse what he's done, but everything's upside-down right now."

Still, Huang, if nothing else, knows how to work a room, Goldberg said.

"Having had the pleasure of trying to pin Jensen down on a live-mic Q&A session at an investor event in the past: Good luck to them," he said of lawmakers' efforts to press Huang for specifics. "He is incredibly charismatic and knows how to handle a microphone."

John Blank, chief equity strategist at Zacks Investment Research, also said Huang was the most personable of the tech titans. But he said Huang understood the gravity of the situation.

"To some degree, he is somewhat humbled from the last two weeks, and I expect him to take it seriously and be pretty straightforward here," Blank said. "I would be surprised if he was flip and super arrogant at this point in time."

Huang's return to the top post - with President Donald Trump's help - launched Nvidia's stock to its biggest one-day percentage gain in 23 years. But shares fell on Tuesday and Wednesday.

Blank said that there may be some investor short-covering during next week's hearings, as investors recalibrate their bets based on any news. But he and other analysts say Nvidia's stock is unlikely to be affected by the hearing, at least in the short-term.

"This is the opening salvo of at least a year of stuff, and the market's pricing in plenty of surprises for all of this," Blank said.

Huang and Nvidia still face investigations from Nvidia's board, Congress and regulators. Trump has said the U.S. government "has no reason to believe that Jensen's return to Nvidia poses any risk" to national security. But more scrutiny could come as Democrats take control of Congress next year.

Democratic Sen. Chuck Schumer, the Senate's current minority leader, has said Democrats would investigate "any wrongdoing" by Nvidia or the Trump administration, and look into discussions between the U.S. and China about Huang, and Trump's Nvidia stock holdings. The White House has said Trump's investment portfolio is managed independently, and that neither Trump nor his family "has any ability to direct, influence, or provide input" on the portfolio, according to multiple reports.

Schumer also called for stronger export controls. Republican Senator John Cornyn of Texas has also criticized Nvidia's decision to bring Huang back to the company.

Other issues still hang over Nvidia's stock, such as the costs and the financing of the AI build-out and Nvidia's role as a financier to other parts of the AI industry. Huang's remarks could pose implications for the broader semiconductor industry, if he happens to reveal more details about the flow of chips into China, Blank said.

The hearings are likely to overshadow Nvidia's GTC conference, which runs from Monday through Thursday. Prior to this month's blowup at the company, Huang was set to deliver the keynote of that event on Tuesday - the same day he appears before the House committees.

According to CNBC, Ian Buck, Nvidia's vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing, was scheduled to speak in place of Huang. Were Huang to make an appearance, analysts said, it could give him a chance to rally the company. But there were also risks.

"It would be lost in the noise and the public spectacle of his return, so I don't know if it would be all that productive for him to be at GTC from a technical standpoint," said Cody Acree, an analyst at StoneX.

Acree said he would be watching for any updates on the rollout of Nvidia's Rubin Ultra chips, seen as a key component of powering agentic AI. Otherwise, it would be an event for networking and discussions about things like copper connectivity.

"Up until very recently, semiconductors were so boring," Goldberg said. "There have been very few instances in which my CEOs ended up in front of Congress. So, brave new world."

-Bill Peters

data.title: Week Ahead for FX, Bonds: Key Labor Data in Focus -2-
data.description:
South Korea is scheduled to release its November trade and inflation data on Tuesday and Wednesday, with exports seen accelerating and consumer price growth easing.

Most analysts expect chip demand fueled by the artificial-intelligence boom to continue driving strong semiconductor exports, further widening the country's trade surplus.

For the first 20 days of November, the country's chip exports nearly quadrupled from a year earlier, keeping them on course for another monthly record.

Citigroup economist Jin-Wook Kim expects South Korea's exports to have climbed 105.4% from a year earlier, faster than revised 93.9% growth in October. He expects the country's trade surplus to widen to $53.6 billion from revised $42.6 billion in the previous month.

Inflation could moderate in November, Kim said in a recent note, as seasonally weaker price pressures from tourism services and agricultural products could outweigh inflationary pressures from pricier durable goods.

Citi expects the headline consumer price index to have risen 2.7% from a year earlier, slower than a 2.8% increase in October. On a monthly basis, the index is seen falling 0.27% after rising 0.25% in October, according to Citi estimates.

Indonesia

Indonesia's November inflation could ease moderately to 3.1% from 3.2% in October, as lower food prices offset some pressure from administered and core components, ANZ's economist Dhiraj Nim said.

Core inflation is expected to remain contained at around 2.6%-2.8%, suggesting price pressures are not yet broad-based. The reading should remain relatively benign for Bank Indonesia, though renewed food-price increases remain a risk, he added.

Resilient exports and a healthy non-oil and gas surplus continue to support Indonesia's trade balance, UOB economist Enrico Tanuwidjaja said. However, imports are growing faster than exports as domestic demand and investment pick up, pointing to a gradual narrowing of the trade surplus, he added.

Southeast Asia

Inflation will be the focus in Southeast Asia during the week, where prices likely eased in November.

The Philippines' headline consumer-price index should ease further in November, reflecting sharp declines in fuel prices, said ING economists. Headline CPI rose 7.8% in October, while core CPI, which excludes volatile food and energy prices, rose 5.4%.

Core CPI likely remained relatively sticky due to still-firm services costs and underlying domestic demand, they added.

Thailand's headline inflation rate likely eased to 3.6% compared to a year ago in November from October's 3.9%, DBS economists said. The expected moderation in prices largely reflected easing energy price pressures, and softer food inflation, they added.

Hong Kong

Hong Kong will report October retail sales on Tuesday. Deutsche Bank Research expects Hong Kong's retail sales value and volume to grow by 5% and 3% year-on-year, respectively, in October, both moderating from September. "The stock market correction may have weighed on local consumer confidence," it says.

Hong Kong's economy has been strong this year. Semiconductor trade and Hong Kong's role in the broader global AI supply chain continued to underpin the city's economic growth, according to a research note by UOB.

Integra Publishes Annual Sustainability Report

Integra Publishes Annual Sustainability Report

PR Newswire

VANCOUVER, BC, Nov. 27, 2026

TSXV: ITR; NYSE American: ITRG
www.integraresources.com

VANCOUVER, BC, Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Integra Resources Corp. ("Integra" or the "Company") (TSXV: ITR) (NYSE American: ITRG) is pleased to announce the publication of its 6th annual Sustainability Report (the "Report") covering the producing Florida Canyon Mine ("Florida Canyon") and the DeLamar Project ("DeLamar") and Nevada North Project ("Nevada North") (together, the "Development Projects"). The Report highlights the Company's first full year as owner and operator of Florida Canyon in northern Nevada and, at DeLamar, the signing of a historic Relationship Agreement with the Shoshone-Paiute Tribes of the Duck Valley Reservation. The Report aligns with the International Financial Reporting Standards ("IFRS") Sustainability Accounting Standards Board ("SASB") Metals and Mining Standard and covers Integra's activities and performance from January 1, 2025 to December 31, 2025.

Environmental, Social, and Governance ("ESG") Highlights:

  • Environmental:
    • Achieved zero reportable spills at Florida Canyon and the Company's Development Projects.
    • Maintained strong water management performance, with no exceedances of water discharge permit limits.
    • Enhanced baselines for stream and wetland mitigation work by surveying approximately 122 acres of wetlands and approximately 116,000 feet of streams at DeLamar.
    • Partnered with Trout Unlimited to explore a potential U.S. Environmental Protection Agency Good Samaritan remediation project for abandoned mine sites in the Jordan Creek watershed, outside DeLamar.
    • Continued support of the Jordan Valley Rangeland Fire Protection Association ("RFPA") and worked in collaboration to combat the threat of rangeland wildfires.
  • Social:
    • Signed the Relationship Agreement with the Shoshone-Paiute Tribes of the Duck Valley Reservation.
    • Integrated all Integra employees into a combined benefits and retirement program.
    • Contributed more than US$400,000 to local communities through donations, sponsorships and in-kind support.
    • Supported over 23,400 people through community programs and strategic investments.
    • Connected with more than 14,500 individuals through meaningful outreach and stakeholder engagement efforts.
    • Incurred one lost-time injury and seven reportable injuries.
    • Implemented a hazard recognition program at Florida Canyon as a leading safety indicator, with more than 300 hazards reported and rectified in December 2025 alone, demonstrating strong workforce adoption.
  • Operations:
    • Advanced a major Florida Canyon fleet expansion, commissioning a Hitachi EX3600 shovel, a CAT 992HL wheel loader, and two new CAT 785 haul trucks in 2025, with six additional CAT 785 haul trucks added to the mining fleet in 2026.
  • Governance:
    • In 2025, 20% of corporate objectives were ESG-linked, and 90% of those objectives were met.

George Salamis, President, CEO and Director of Integra commented: "2025 was a defining year for Integra. In our first full year operating Florida Canyon, we began to establish a mining operation built on our values, investing in the people, equipment and systems needed to sustain the mine in the years ahead.  At DeLamar, years of meaningful engagement culminated in a Relationship Agreement with the Shoshone-Paiute Tribes of the Duck Valley Reservation, a milestone we are particularly proud of. Together, these achievements reflect our commitment to responsible mining and building lasting relationships with the communities where we operate. As we continue towards our goal of becoming a mid-tier precious metals producer, we remain committed to accountability, environmental stewardship and the well-being of our people and communities."

The 2025 Sustainability Report is available on Integra's website using the following link:

https://integraresources.com/esg/esg-reporting/

About Integra Resources

Integra is a growing precious metals producer in the Great Basin of the Western United States. Integra is focused on demonstrating profitability and operational excellence at its principal operating asset, the Florida Canyon Mine, located in Nevada. In addition, Integra is committed to advancing its flagship development-stage heap leach projects: the past producing DeLamar Project located in southwestern Idaho and the Nevada North Project located in western Nevada. Integra creates sustainable value for shareholders, stakeholders, and local communities through successful mining operations, efficient project development, disciplined capital allocation, and strategic M&A, while upholding the highest industry standards for environmental, social, and governance practices.

data.title: EON Resources Inc. Reports Theft to New Mexico Oilfield Theft Task Force Resulting in Quick Action
data.description:
HOUSTON, TX / ACCESS Newswire / November 27, 2026 / EON Resources Inc. (NYSE American:EONR) ("EON" or the "Company") is an independent upstream energy company with 20,000 leasehold acres in the Permian Basin with approximately 1.2 billion barrels of original oil in place. Today, the Company announced that it reported a theft of property from the oil field to the New Mexico Oilfield Theft Task Force (the "NMOTTF") that led to arrests of several suspects.

On Saturday, November 21, 2026, at approximately 3:00 am, three suspects wearing dark masks, in a blue pickup, were caught on security cameras at the Grayburg-Jackson oil field in Eddy County, New Mexico owned and operated by LH Operating, LLC, a wholly owned subsidiary of EON. The suspects cut and stole copper wire critical to some of the field's operations.

"Each of the perpetrators were wearing masks, but the Company had good surveillance video including video of the pickup truck involved. All video and photographs were turned over to the SE New Mexico Oilfield Theft Task Force," said Dante Caravaggio, CEO of EON. EON also posted the same photographs on social media hoping someone would recognize and help identify the pickup and individuals. A Good Samaritan reported individuals and a vehicle matching the description from the surveillance footage. With the volunteered information turned over to the NMOTTF, the NMOTTF arrived at a residence where a truck was located fitting the description of the truck used in the theft and arrests were made.

According to authorities, a significant amount of copper wire was identified at the residence. The copper wire had been stripped of its insulation.

The NMOTTF moved quickly to identify alleged participants within two days of the theft. Limited production in the field was partially interrupted for 3 days until new wire could be procured and installed on a fast-track basis.

"We are thrilled to have reported the theft directly to the New Mexico Oilfield Theft Task Force who were incredible. We hope cameras and quick action, as was the case this time, help all operators bring down costs, downtime, and losses from criminal activity that hurts everyone," stated Dante Caravaggio.

About EON Resources Inc.

EON is an independent upstream energy company focused on maximizing total returns to shareholders through the development of onshore oil and natural gas properties. EON's Class A Common Stock trades on the NYSE American under "EONR," and its public warrants trade under "EONR WS." For more information on the Company, please visit the EON website.

Two Permian Basin Assets, Multiple Development Horizons

Grayburg-Jackson Field (GJF): 13,700 contiguous leasehold acres in Eddy County, New Mexico, with stacked pay zones and almost 1 billion barrels of estimated original oil in place, of which less than 7% has been produced to date. The San Andres horizontal development program commenced in August 2026.

South Justis Unit (SJU): 5,360 contiguous acres in Lea County, New Mexico, with approximately 207 million barrels of original oil in place. EON's geologic and reservoir work on the Blinebry zone indicates development potential that management believes is similar in character to the opportunity identified in the GJF.

data.title: Inflation Slides in France, Spain on Declining Fuel Prices — 4th Update
data.description:
By Ed Frankl and Paul Hannon

The annual rate of inflation in France and Spain fell more sharply than expected in November as fuel prices declined, while the eurozone economy grew less rapidly than previously estimated in the three months through September.

Investors expect the European Central Bank to raise its key interest rate next month for a third time since the start of the war between the U.S. and Iran. But the central bank has said it will be "data-dependent" in its policy decisions, and the latest readings from the eurozone economy point to weaker inflationary pressures.

Consumer prices in the eurozone's second-largest economy were 3.2% higher than in the same month of 2025, a lower annual rate of inflation than the 3.7% recorded in October, France's statistics office said Friday. Economists polled last week by The Wall Street Journal expected a 3.6% rate of inflation.

In Spain, figures published Friday showed the annual rate of inflation also dropped sharply in November, to 4.1% from 4.9% in October.

Oil prices have fallen since the outcome of U.S. midterm elections fueled hopes of a lasting resolution to the conflict, although they remain above prewar levels. As a result, prices of gasoline and other fuels have declined.

However, European natural gas prices remain near multiyear highs, which will keep household energy prices elevated throughout the colder winter months.

The ECB has raised its key rate twice so far this year, judging that the surge in energy prices was too great to ignore. Investors are primed for another hike before the end of the year.

The EU said last week that it expects French inflation to peak at 4.3% in the first quarter of 2027 due to further increases in energy prices and how they pass through into food and services.

Yet incoming data shows few signs of those energy costs spilling over into other parts of the economy. Services inflation in France fell in November due to a sharp decrease in prices for accommodation and transport services.

Revised figures for economic growth in the three months through September indicate that the eurozone economy has been less resilient in the face of higher energy prices than previously estimated.

The French statistics agency on Friday said the country's gross domestic product sank 0.2% in the third quarter, having previously estimated the drop at 0.1%. Consumer spending was also flat in October. Surveys of purchasing managers for November showed steady economic growth in Germany, while there was a deepening downturn in activity in France.

"A weakening labor market and growing fears of unemployment will keep households cautious. At the same time, weak demand and a lack of visibility will continue to weigh on business investment. The outlook for 2027 remains very gloomy," Charlotte de Montpellier, an economist at ING, wrote in a note to clients.

Earlier this week, Germany's statistics agency cut its estimate for third-quarter growth. Meanwhile, eurozone business sentiment slipped this month, according to separate data published Friday.

Amid those signs of weakening inflationary pressures, the ECB's own survey of 19,000 consumers between Oct. 1 and Nov. 2 yielded some concerning news for policymakers. It found that households expected prices to rise by 3.5% over the coming 12 months, up from 3.1% in September.

However, expectations may fall back in response to November's inflation figures, although the next survey won't be released until early next year and the ECB announces its policy decision on Dec. 17.

data.title: Meituan Posts Earnings Beat as Price War Cools — Update
data.description:
By Tracy Qu

Meituan's profit stabilized amid accelerating revenue growth as China's top food-delivery company continued to recover from a brutal price war.

The results suggest that the worst is over for the Beijing-based company, which has battled Alibaba Group and JD.com for more than a year to defend its food-delivery market share.

Competition has eased in recent quarters, helping Meituan return to profit in the April to June period and beat market expectations in the third quarter.

The Chinese shopping-and-delivery platform on Friday said net profit was 2.07 billion yuan, equivalent to $310.7 million, largely stable from the previous quarter.

Revenue climbed 22% from a year earlier, faster than growth of 14% in the second quarter and 5.6% in the first three months of the year.

Analysts have said that Meituan's market leadership in China's local-services sector and efficiency edge against competitors could support its recovery once competition normalizes.

Fitch Ratings earlier indicated that Meituan's recovery trajectory was intact. It also flagged the company's faster reduction of food-delivery losses in recent quarters compared with late last year, suggesting that even a modest easing in subsidy intensity can materially improve profitability.

Indeed, the profit recovery in its core local commerce segment helped push total operating profit 1.8% higher sequentially in the third quarter.

Meituan's core business revenue rose 17% from a year ago, while revenue from new initiatives, which include overseas businesses, climbed 33%.

The company noted an inflection point in the food-delivery industry in the third quarter. "Industry subsidies grew increasingly rational after the summer promotion season," it said.

Meituan's international business also maintained robust growth momentum. Keeta further improved its profit margin in Hong Kong and achieved profitability in Saudi Arabia for the quarter, it said.

Yet challenges remain for the company. Citi analysts flagged seasonal factors and colder weather as headwinds that could weigh on rider costs in the fourth quarter. Still, continued spending discipline and operational efficiency from Meituan should support sequential improvement in unit economics, they said in a note.

Meituan shares rose 8.2% in Hong Kong ahead of the results amid broader sector gains, helping pare losses this year to about 34%.

data.title: I hate that Jensen Huang is back at Nvidia, but I love what it's done for my 401(k). Am I a hypocrite?
data.description:
By Quentin Fottrell

Doing nothing and maintaining an even temperament is often the work of gods

Jensen Huang, who on Monday returned as CEO of Nvidia. (Photo subject is a model.)

Dear Quentin,

I was paralyzed during the market downturn, so I have a question in the event that this bounce - led by the shocking and, in my opinion, unwelcome news that Jensen Huang has returned as Nvidia's (NVDA) CEO - does not last. No comment on that, as it happens, even though I have my opinions, like most people do.

I'm writing to you about my own strategy, not to pass judgment on other people's corporate decisions. During a market downturn, is it better for me to draw down cash from CDs for the next year or two rather than taking money from my equities and annuities at a loss? Where are the safe havens? I don't want to eat into my retirement savings.

Planning Ahead

You can email The Moneyist with any financial and ethical questions at qfottrell@marketwatch.com. The Moneyist regrets he cannot reply to questions individually.

Related: America is divided into two countries - Trump's pro-billionaires and Mamdani's anti-billionaires

Being paralyzed during the recent volatility in the market is not exactly a bad thing.

Dear Planning,

It's fair to say that many people were surprised by Jensen Huang's return on Monday - and you are not alone in having strong opinions on that.

Some of the same people who cried foul over the fall in their 401(k)s and IRAs may well be rolling their eyes over the return of Huang to the helm of Nvidia, which now appears to be the cornerstone of the AI revolution, mostly due to its multibillion-dollar microchip business and proprietary software ecosystem. Indeed, the stock gave up some of Monday's gains on Tuesday as investors turned their attention to regulatory concerns about the export of U.S. microchips to China and elsewhere. Huang was effectively fired (he officially resigned) from the company a couple of weeks ago over his reported affairs with two employees, as well as one with a woman who has been accused of being a Chinese spy.

Commentators have questioned whether President Donald Trump overlooked the potential and alleged national-security threat by calling for Huang's return to Nvidia NVDA, thereby signaling that the company is too big to fail. Others bemoaned the decision by the company's board and wondered what the role of such boards is, if not to uphold professional, legal and personal standards. While low-wage American workers have been fired over bathroom breaks, skeptics may wonder if rules of conduct only apply to nonbillionaires.

It's OK to have joys and concerns about the billionaire class and your 401(k), even if the answers conflict with each other.

And, honestly, being paralyzed during the recent volatility in the market is not exactly a bad thing, either. Doing nothing and maintaining an even temperament is often the work of gods. Some people panic and sell, or move into real estate, bonds, or gold, and constantly check their 401(k) while getting upset over paper losses. Yet short-term swings won't have a big impact if they aren't about to retire or haven't just retired - especially if they have cash alternatives. How many times a day or week did you check your 401(k) when the market was on the rise? I'm guessing not a lot.

I sympathize with your urge to check. According to a 2026 report by the Investment Company Institute (ICI), a global trade association representing regulated funds and their shareholders, 81% of mutual fund-owning U.S. households hold stock funds - most of them inside workplace retirement plans. Because broad stock and index funds are heavily weighted toward mega-cap AI leaders like Nvidia, a significant share of American households are naturally exposed to those stocks. "Mutual funds play a key role in their households' balance sheets," the researchers wrote.

But back to the other questions in your letter: Yes, drawing from CDs and relying on annuity income can be a smart move. That assumes you don't have required minimum distributions from a traditional retirement account and your CDs have reached the end of their term. If you paid extra for a guaranteed lifetime income rider on your annuities - locking in an income stream if markets plummet or your account balance falls to zero - that will protect you during a correction, while fixed annuities aren't tied to the market's fortunes at all. Having cash alternatives helps you avoid "sequence-of-returns risk," where poor market performance in the early years of retirement puts pressure on a portfolio you're drawing from.

Don't miss: 'Nvidia's turmoil has me spooked': Is it time to sell my stocks and buy real estate?

Timing the market vs. managing risk

Darius Dale, founder and CEO of 42 Macro, a macroeconomic research and systematic risk-management firm, predicts that markets will return to a "risk-on market regime," where investors favor higher risk assets over safe havens, within a couple of months. "Hope is not an effective risk-management process," he says. "Positioning for the market regime helps investors avoid fear of missing out (FOMO) and fear of more losses (FOML). FOMO causes investors to buy cycle tops, and FOML causes investors to sell cycle lows. These are the two worst things any investor can do to their financial well-being."

As for your curiosity about safe havens, I can understand why you would consider them after such a volatile week, especially with lingering questions about the stock market's heavy dependence on AI. The right mix depends on your risk tolerance and, as Dale suggested, your expectations about the economic outlook, especially if you want to factor in how reliant the economy is becoming on AI. There are many paths to take. Andrew Clinton, CEO of Clinton Investment Management, suggests municipal bonds as a haven during a correction.

I can understand why you would look for safe havens, especially with lingering questions about the market's heavy dependence on AI.

Municipal bonds are, for the record, more appropriate for investors in higher tax brackets with money held in taxable accounts who live in high-tax states, and for retirees prioritizing cash flow and capital preservation. "Municipal bonds offer attractive tax-adjusted carry and stable underlying asset-class credit quality for investors seeking durable cash flows amidst equity-market volatility," he says. "Current municipal bond yields remain near the most attractive levels in decades."

Clinton also has a rosier outlook on the underlying strength of the U.S. economy than, perhaps, many folks. "Credit fundamentals remain strong, with default rates representing only a fraction of corporate default rates," he says. "Municipal issuers provide essential services such as airports, utilities and toll roads, generating durable cash flows with limited exposure to corporate earnings volatility. If inflation moderates and rates decline, municipals offer the potential for both attractive income and capital appreciation."

For other safe havens, consider shorter-duration bonds, mutual funds and exchange-traded funds that invest in bonds with maturities of less than five years, as well as Treasury inflation-protected securities (TIPS) backed by the U.S. Treasury to guard against rising prices. Give a thought to value-oriented and defensive sectors, including consumer-staples, utilities and healthcare stocks, for retired investors who seek stability over higher returns. Your lifestyle, the balances in your retirement accounts, your goals, your financial profile - whether you have a mortgage, debt or long-term-care insurance - and your views on AI all play a role.

Pausing during a storm does not mean you suffer from paralysis, and you don't have to like the news in order to plan around it.

Your letter attests to that.

Related: Is Social Security a Ponzi scheme? No. Don't get carried away with 1930s-era prophecies of doom.

data.title: VistaJet and The Cultivist Open Miami Art Week with a Private Morning at The Bass
data.description:
VistaJet and The Cultivist Open Miami Art Week with a Private Morning at The Bass

VistaJet and The Cultivist Open Miami Art Week with a Private Morning at The Bass

PR Newswire

MIAMI, Nov. 27, 2026

 An invitation-only breakfast and private tour bringing together 100 collectors, artists and cultural leaders from around the world. 

MIAMI, Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- On Tuesday, December 1, VistaJet and The Cultivist will open Miami Art Week with an intimate, invitation-only morning at The Bass in Miami Beach, welcoming guests to the museum's Lindemann Courtyard ahead of the Design Miami VIP opening. The gathering will begin with breakfast, followed by private, small-group tours of Sarah Zapata's exhibition, Against a State of Malevolence, before the museum opens to the public.

VistaJet and The Cultivist share a mission: to connect individuals with in-person, culturally enriching experiences. VistaJet Members share a deep passion for art and culture, a natural fit with The Cultivist's philosophy: "Art unlocks life. We unlock art." Through this collaboration, VistaJet will bring collectors together from across the globe to form meaningful connections and immerse themselves in Sarah Zapata's captivating world of textiles.

For VistaJet, the journey is part of the experience. Inspired by the golden age of flying, VistaJet has spent more than two decades pioneering a new standard in global business aviation, flying its Members anytime, anywhere, to the world's cultural capitals, from Miami to Basel and beyond. This is the Art of Flying: every journey a gateway to art and culture.

Against a State of Malevolence envelops visitors in the textile environments of Sarah Zapata (b. 1988) that unfold through color, texture, scale, and movement. A builder of worlds, Zapata draws from weaving traditions, architecture, queer identity, and her Peruvian heritage, transforming textiles into emotional objects that are at once tactile, monumental, and symbolic. Through weaving, tufting, and sewing, she creates installations that invite viewers not only to look at, but to move through.

Leona Qi, President, U.S. at VistaJet: "Some of my favorite conversations with our Members are about the art they've discovered on their travels. Many are passionate collectors who travel the world for art, and Miami Art Week is one of the moments that brings them together. With The Cultivist, we're opening the door to something truly special: a private morning at The Bass, and a rare chance to discover extraordinary work together, alongside the artist herself."

Marlies Verhoeven, CEO and Co-Founder of The Cultivist: "We are thrilled to partner with VistaJet to bring together the international arts community for the start of Miami Art Week, and celebrate Sarah Zapata's incredible work with our friends at The Bass. Our mission is to extend access to the most novel and influential arts experiences globally, and VistaJet's services make that possible. There is no replacement for the sensorial experience of visiting art in person."

Guests will be greeted with a welcome drink before opening remarks and a family-style breakfast. Marlies Verhoeven and Leona Qi will introduce the partnership, followed by comments from Silvia Karman Cubiñá, the executive director and chief curator at The Bass. Guests will then hear from the artist herself, as Sarah Zapata speaks to her process and vision behind Against a State of Malevolence. Once the breakfast concludes, the guests will split into small groups and embark on their private tours. The intimate setting will allow each guest to get lost in Zapata's world of textiles. Every element of the morning has been considered with care, from artist-inspired tablescapes in a palette of white, green and burgundy to subtle touches of VistaJet hospitality, reflecting the same thoughtfulness and attention to detail that VistaJet Members experience on board.

The Bass, Miami Beach's contemporary art museum, has been active since 1964 and resides in the former Miami Beach Public Library. The 1930s Art Deco building, designed by Russell Pancoast, is the perfect home for international contemporary art, blending tradition with innovation. In 2001, architect Arata Isozaki reimagined this space, expanding the galleries by 16,000 square feet and allowing for the inclusion of rotating temporary exhibitions.

About VistaJet

VistaJet is the first and only global business aviation company. On the unrivaled Vista Members' fleet, VistaJet has flown corporations, governments and private clients to over 200 countries and territories, covering 96% of the world.

Founded over 20 years ago, the company pioneered an innovative business model where customers are granted access to an entire fleet while paying only for the hours they fly, free of the responsibilities and asset risks linked to aircraft ownership and fractional ownership.

VistaJet's signature Program membership offers customers a bespoke subscription of flight hours on its fleet of mid and long-range jets, to fly them with as little as 24 hours' notice.

VistaJet is part of Vista Global Holding (Vista) — the world's leading private aviation group, headquartered at the DIFC in Dubai, integrating a unique portfolio of companies offering asset free solutions to cover all key aspects of business aviation.

More VistaJet information and news at www.vistajet.com

"Vista" is a trade name for Vista Global Holding Limited. Vista does not operate any aircraft. All flights are performed by properly licensed operators, which may include VistaJet Limited or VistaJet GmbH as well as FAA-licensed and DOT registered US direct air carriers Western Air Charter, Inc. and Jet Select, LLC (each DBA Vista America).

About The Cultivist

Founded in 2015, The Cultivist is a private art membership club and creative agency with offices in New York, Dallas, Miami, London, and Los Angeles.

For our members, we provide enlightening resources, enriching experiences, and concierge services to make living an art-filled life effortless. And for brands and businesses, we combine deep expertise and an unmatched network to create captivating art-led activations. 

The Cultivist is independent, focusing on education and access instead of selling art — which means we've earned a high level of trust in the market, and from our hundreds of museum, gallery, and creative partners around the world.

For more information about The Cultivist visit TheCultivist.com.
